style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression, asymmetric off-centre composition: one isolated weathered shipping container behind a chain-link customs hold fence on a container terminal quay, lower-left, the main stack receding right. Low raking golden-hour sunlight from the left cuts hard shadows across corrugated steel and asphalt, palette graphite, safety yellow and weathered orange. Crisp high contrast, stacked gantry cranes silhouetted behind, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, illegible numbers
rationale: Scale makes the custody consequence physical: telephoto compression stacks the port's throughput against the one container pulled out of flow, and long-lens clarity shows the terminal as the clock-owning environment.
subject: a weathered shipping container isolated behind a chain-link customs hold fence at a container terminal
core_thesis: An import shipment runs on customs deadlines the control tower does not own, so the escalation rule has to be computed from the entry's own timestamps, not from the carrier milestone feed.
core_conflict: Carrier milestone feed vs. customs entry deadlines (security filing, 15-day entry, general-order, liquidation, protest) where a missed entry removes freight from the commercial chain into port custody.
composition: 200mm telephoto compression, asymmetric off-centre composition with the isolated container lower-left, stacked terminal receding right
alt_text: A weathered shipping container behind a chain-link customs fence on a container terminal, with gantry cranes and stacked boxes in low light.
caption: 15-DAY Entry Gap Then Custody: Miss the 15-day entry deadline and the freight enters Customs custody, risk and expense.
title: 15-DAY Entry Gap Then Custody
